html:
SMTO-SKL-0159 — Your GitHub token isn't allowed to do this

GUID: dbadb70d-6046-5d41-b897-06b9d38f78f3
Slug: github-permission-missing
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • The saved GitHub account doesn't have permission for what you asked, either by the permissions recorded in SMTO or because GitHub refused. Nothing was changed on GitHub.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in the conversation which GitHub permission the blocked step needed, for example write access to Issues. The step's result names the exact permission missing, so you don't grant more than needed.
  2. On github.com, edit your token so it has that permission for this repository. If the repository belongs to an organization, make sure the organization has approved the token. GitHub decides what the token may do; SMTO can't add access itself.
  3. In Parameter Store, open your GitHub account entry, select Reveal & edit value, add the same permission to the granted permissions, and select Save. SMTO checks the permissions recorded here before it contacts GitHub.
  4. For notifications only: create a classic GitHub token with the notifications or repo scope, save it as the token, set the credential type to classic_pat and add that scope to the granted scopes. GitHub doesn't give notifications to fine-grained tokens, so only a classic token works here.

What success looks like

  • Repeating your request completes without a permission error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or the GitHub organization owner. Only grant the permission this action needs, and don't paste tokens into the chat.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The GitHub permission check failed: the profile's declared fine-grained permissions do not cover the operation, a notification tool lacks a classic PAT with notifications/repo scope, or GitHub returned a non-rate-limit 403.

What this means

  • Declared fine-grained permissions or notification PAT compatibility fail preflight, or GitHub returns a non-rate-limit HTTP 403 outside the branch-protection case. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • Declared fine-grained permissions or notification PAT compatibility fail preflight, or GitHub returns a non-rate-limit HTTP 403 outside the branch-protection case.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect required/accepted permission alternatives, repository selection and organization/SSO policy.

How to fix it

  • See details.feature and required_permission_sets or accepted_permission_sets: within a set every permission is required, separate sets are alternatives. Grant the missing permission for the exact repository on the PAT (and organization/SSO approval if required), then update granted_permissions in the GitHub Account profile; notification tools need credential_type classic_pat with notifications or repo in granted_scopes, since fine-grained PATs are unsupported. Never widen access automatically.
  • Authorize the named feature for the exact account and selected repository. Use required_permission_sets or accepted_permission_sets: commas mean all permissions, alternatives mean any one set. For notifications only, explicitly configure classic PAT compatibility with notifications or repo scope; fine-grained PATs are unsupported. Obtain organization/SSO approval where required. Never widen access automatically.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The explicitly intended account meets the actual feature and repository requirements without automatically widening access.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
